public_rationale: Both parts hold. On losses: Anthropic's prospectus, as reported by Reuters, shows a 2025 net loss of $42 billion and an operating loss of more than $8 billion even excluding a financing-related charge. A later draft shows an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026. That is billions of dollars a year on any reading. On growth: Anthropic said paid Claude subscriptions more than doubled in early 2026, the same period in which it tightened peak-hour limits to manage demand. Reuters reported that revenue more than doubled from Q1 to Q2 2026. Anthropic kept accepting subscribers, and growth continued despite the capacity problems.
limitations: Figures are from a draft prospectus, not an audited public filing.
Most of the net loss is a non-cash accounting charge; the operating loss is the more conservative measure.
'Not affecting its growth' cannot be shown precisely; continued strong growth is the evidence.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic is losing billions of dollars a year while its capacity issues do not affect its subscriber growth.

statement.excerpt: Anthropic is currently losing billions of dollars a year offering a service with amateurish availability and oscillating quality, and continues to accept new subscribers, meaning that capacity issues are not affecting its growth.

from_speaker: currently losing billions of dollars a year
capacity issues are not affecting its growth
our_interpretation: Plain reading of 'losing billions of dollars a year': Anthropic's annual loss, as the company reports it, is in the billions of dollars. Both net loss and operating loss are relevant.

'Currently' with 'a year' is ongoing. Target period: the latest full year before the post (2025) plus the half-year containing the post (January to June 2026), the periods public evidence reports on. This choice is mine.

Plain reading of the second part: despite capacity problems, Anthropic kept signing up subscribers and its growth continued. It does not require capacity problems to have had zero effect on any customer.
criteria.support_condition: Company figures showing an annual or half-year loss of billions of dollars, together with evidence that subscribers and revenue kept growing during the capacity problems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Figures showing losses below a billion dollars a year, or evidence that subscriber signups or growth stalled or reversed because of capacity limits.
